mainEntity.name: How many ads should I test at once?

acceptedAnswer.text: Few enough that each can collect meaningful results on your budget. Testing many ads with little spend gives noisy answers.

mainEntity.name: How do I know an ad is winning?

acceptedAnswer.text: Read cost per purchase against your break-even ROAS, then confirm the result in a second round.

mainEntity.name: How often should I refresh creative?

acceptedAnswer.text: When signs of fatigue appear, such as rising frequency and a rising cost per purchase. Have the next round ready before that point.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: Creative testing is the practice of running different ads against each other in a controlled way, so you learn which hook, angle or format works instead of guessing.

paras: On paid social, the ad is often what decides whether someone stops, and the targeting matters less than it used to. That makes creative one of the main things a brand controls. Without a system, teams make ads on instinct and cannot say why one worked.
A testing system turns each ad into a lesson. Over a few rounds you build a clear picture of which hooks, angles and formats work for your buyers.
blocks.cap: Each concept carries one clear idea, so results can be read.

list: Hook: the first seconds or first line that stops the scroll.
Angle: the reason to buy, such as a problem solved, a result, a comparison or social proof.
Format: creator video, product demo, static image, carousel.
Offer: bundle, discount or free shipping, tested separately from the creative idea.

steps.d: For example, does a problem-first hook beat a product-first hook?

steps.t: Make variants that differ in one way
steps.d: Keep everything else the same so the difference can be read.
Agree the budget, the length and the metric before the test starts, so the result is not judged after the fact.
Run tests in their own campaign, then move winners into your scaling campaigns.
Write down what won and the reason you think it won, so the next round starts smarter.

blocks.cap: A testing campaign compares several ads against the same goal.

blocks.h: Spend the most time on the hook
paras: For video, the first three seconds decide whether the rest is watched. Test several openings of the same video before you test whole new videos. It is faster and cheaper, and it shows what earns attention.

Read hook performance on how many people keep watching, and read the ad as a whole on cost per purchase. An ad that gets attention but does not sell needs a different message, not a different opening.
blocks.cap: Editing several openings of the same video makes hooks easy to compare.

paras: Judge ads on cost per purchase read against your break-even ROAS, not on clicks or likes. Use attention measures such as hold rate to work out why an ad won or lost.

Be careful with small samples. A result from a handful of purchases can change with more spend, so let each test collect enough results before you call a winner, and confirm the winner in a second round. Also remember that platforms over-count, so compare ads against each other inside one platform.
Ads wear out as the same people see them again and again. Signs include rising frequency, falling click-through and a rising cost per purchase for the same ad.
Plan the next round of creative before the current winners tire. Keep the winning idea and change the hook, the creator or the format, so the ad feels new without losing what worked.
blocks.cap: Frequency rising while click-through falls is a common sign of fatigue.
